tickets.text:
Intermittent DNS resolution failures for internal services

Users in the Chicago office were trying to reach internal services by the hostname svc.internal.corp, but DNS resolution intermittently returned different A records after a same-day zone edit performed by network engineer David Kowalski (emp ID NE-40821). Some clients resolved the new address 10.10.5.21 and connected successfully, while others received the previous IP 10.10.4.9 and application requests to internal endpoints failed by name. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (mchen@corplabs.com) at approximately 15:00 UTC. Impact was limited to internal services in corp-datacenter-1 and caused inconsistent connectivity and elevated DNS lookup failures in Network Monitoring dashboards.

input.next_step: Investigate the DNS cache state and potential replication delays for the internal corp-datacenter-1 zone.
input.rationale: The reported issue involves intermittent DNS resolution failures across subnets following a zone update, which aligns with symptoms of a stale resolver cache in the corporate DNS infrastructure. As per the internal DNS playbook, resolution of such issues is exclusively managed by the network team and is outside the scope of L1 support.
input.ruled_out: Stale zone record; Broken conditional forwarder. These are identified as possibilities but cannot be ruled out without access to the network infrastructure's zone files and forwarder configuration, which are reserved for the network engineering team.
input.summary: Intermittent DNS resolution failures for svc.internal.corp reported following a zone update in corp-datacenter-1.

The issue was first reported by Maria Gonzalez (emp ID E20481) at the Phoenix office around 06:15 UTC, who noticed her documents to the HR-Floor2-Queue were not printing. The issue affected Sales and HR printing workflows on the Windows Server 2019 print server PDQ-Print01, preventing normal document output from department queues including \\PDQ-Print01\Sales-Main and \\PDQ-Print01\HR-Floor2-Queue.

input.rationale: The issue is confirmed as 'Driver unavailable' across multiple queues on the print server PDQ-Print01, which is a server-side infrastructure issue. Per the printing KB, 'Driver unavailable' across a queue requires a driver reinstallation, but the provided tools are limited to PS-PRINT01, whereas the affected server is PDQ-Print01. Escalating to SD-PRINT as they own print server queues and drivers.
input.summary: Multiple print queues on server PDQ-Print01 are reporting 'Driver unavailable' errors, affecting Sales and HR departments.
input.next_step: Investigate and resolve the driver corruption on PDQ-Print01.
